o1.biggest_strength: Three fixes ranked by money saved with the working shown, and every message written in our voice with one button each.
o1.biggest_mistake: Sales-kept figure (£75.7k–£129.7k) is a bit high relative to the modest refund-share move and could over-promise the owner.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the SMS option on day 3 (cheap, higher open rate than email) and a small per-audience breakdown of which bra styles drive 'too small', so the fit-page work has a target.

o2.biggest_strength: Six messages including a day-3 'nearly there' email+SMS and a delivered email with real bra-fit guidance, plus feeding size reasons back to product pages.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 'up to £183,800 sales kept' from a 82%→65% refund move on all returns is not credible for an owner and muddies an otherwise sharp plan.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the swap maths conservatively (only size-related returns, £58 partial) and commit to a single refund-share target rather than a wide 'up to' figure.

reason: Both are genuinely usable; output 1 wins on the numbers and how confidently it defends them, which is what I would act on, though I want output 2's day-3 SMS and delivered-fit guidance folded in.
